chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Fistfight with Walter Kay over marbles
summary: A fight with his friend Walter Kay ends with their teacher whipping them and making them kiss in front of the class.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. I remember that very well. Because I had some friends in school, and they -- his name was Walter Kay, see, very good friends.
And we got in a big argument in school. And so I told him, When you come outside, I'm going to whip your head and all like that. When we went outside,

we got in this big fight, see, fist fight, now. All the kids was around, and we was just fighting like cats and dogs. So one of the teachers came up, my teacher, Mrs. Gardiner, came up and caught both of us and pulled us apart.

And said, 'Now, both of you go inside.' So we went inside. But when recess was over, we was sitting in one corner, -- I'm in one corner, he's in another, see. And when all the kids came in, she made us come up front of the class and she gave us a good shellacking. And on top of that, she made us kiss.
And, oh, boy, I'd rather have taken the whipping than kiss him.
And the kids just fell out, see.
What a funny thing. You were razzed about that for years, I bet.
I had to kiss him? Oh, no, gee.
What was the fight over, do you remember?
I don't know, the marbles, it was, really, you see.
And he was a good friend?

Oh, sure, a good friend of mine. And the next time I saw him was in Houston, Texas, I think. We sat down and talked about this, and laugh. We had to hug and kiss. And she made us kiss right on the mouth, too. It wasn't no cheek.
